extracted.intended_audience: investigators and applicants preparing or revising NIH grant proposals (including trainees and faculty)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applicants on interpreting an NIH Summary Statement (impact score, reviewer critiques, budget notes) and deciding whether and how to revise and resubmit a proposal. Focuses on assessing repairability of reviewer concerns and using recommended strategies to prepare a resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary statement will include your overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented in the Summary Statement as the primary numeric evaluation of the application; use it as a starting point to gauge reviewer consensus about the application's overall merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Summary Statement will list strengths and weaknesses identified by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the enumerated strengths and weaknesses to identify what to preserve and what to revise in a resubmission; they are the core reviewer feedback items to address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Areas of concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will note specific 'areas of concern' about the proposal in the Summary Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat areas of concern as priority problems to evaluate for repairability before deciding to resubmit; these often drive the review outcome more than minor critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended budget
rubrics_metrics.description: The Summary Statement may include a recommended budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the recommended budget with your requested budget and consider revising cost justifications or scope if reviewers flagged budgetary issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific review officer synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Most summary statements include a short synopsis based on peer reviewer critiques, prepared by a scientific review officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the SRO synopsis for a concise framing of reviewer consensus and to clarify the most salient concerns to address in an amended submission or rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess whether proposal problems are repairable
rubrics_metrics.description: When a proposal is not funded, it is important to assess whether proposal problems are repairable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the nature and extent of reviewer concerns (e.g., fixable methodological details vs. fundamental conceptual flaws) to decide if revision can realistically address the critiques for the next round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide whether to resubmit in the next round
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether it’s in your best interest to resubmit your proposal in the next round after reviewing the Summary Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a strategic decision based on repairability, timeline, funding portfolio, and whether revisions would substantially improve the application's competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use expert-reviewed strategies to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: This section (and accompanying video) covers strategies for successfully responding to an NIH Summary Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the recommended resources (e.g., the Elizabeth Samelson video) for concrete tactics on how to interpret critiques, prioritize revisions, and craft a resubmission or rebuttal.
